<timestamp>Saturday, Nov 14, 2026, 6:38 PM (UTC+8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
If a CTA section is required, in the markdown document, then how ? 
</user_query>
I'll look up how required CTA sections are modeled for markdown content in this project.

input.command: entire search "CTA section required markdown" --json 2>&1 | head -80; entire agent-help search 2>&1 | head -40
input.description: Search Entire for CTA section context

content.text:
In the current marketing template, a CTA is **not** part of the markdown. Landing CTAs live in `src/components/sections/Cta.astro` and are pulled into `index.astro`. Blog/help `.md` files only have their own schemas (`title`, `description`, etc.) — no CTA field.

If you want a **required CTA on a markdown entry**, put it in that collection’s Zod schema as required frontmatter, then fill it in the Fields panel (or YAML):

```ts
cta: z.object({
  heading: z.string(),
  label: z.string(),
  href: z.string(),
}),
```

```yaml
---
title: Launch day
cta:
  heading: Ready to launch?
  label: Get started
  href: /pricing
---
```

Orso treats that like any other required field: it shows in **Fields** with `*`, and save fails until it’s set. The markdown **body** stays prose; the CTA data stays in frontmatter (or a section variant if you use a discriminated `section` / `sections` union).

So: required CTA in markdown → schema + frontmatter. Landing-page CTA in this template → edit the Astro section, not a `.md` file.

<timestamp>Saturday, Nov 14, 2026, 6:43 PM (UTC+8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
The CTA can be at the top middle or any way 
</user_query>

If the CTA can sit at the top, middle, or anywhere, don’t model it as one fixed page field. Model it as an **ordered section** so position comes from order, not from a special “CTA slot.”

**Page sections (landing-style)**  
Store an ordered list and let `cta` be one variant:

```yaml
---
title: Home
sections:
  - type: hero
    heading: …
  - type: cta
    label: Get started
    href: /pricing
  - type: features
    …
---
```

Or separate section entries with `order`. The page just renders `sections` in order — CTA wherever it appears (first, middle, last, or more than once).

**Inside an article body**  
Use MDX and drop the component inline:

```mdx
Intro paragraph…

<Cta heading="Ready?" label="Get started" href="/pricing" />

More prose…
```

That puts the CTA anywhere in the reading flow.

**Rule of thumb:** fixed footer CTA → one frontmatter object or a hardcoded Astro section. CTA that can move → ordered sections or an inline MDX component, not a single required top-level `cta` field.

<timestamp>Saturday, Nov 14, 2026, 6:44 PM (UTC+8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
If that's the case, my existing markdown preview will no longer work right ? 
</user_query>
I'll check how the current markdown preview is wired so we can see what a flexible CTA model would break.

Mostly no — it depends how you place the CTA.

**Ordered sections in frontmatter** (CTA as a `type: cta` block in a list): your existing markdown body preview/editor keeps working. The body stays normal `.md`. The CTA is edited in **Fields**, and the live site **Preview** shows it wherever that list puts it.

**Inline MDX in the body** (`<Cta … />` mid-article): that *does* break the rich markdown editor. Orso already treats MDX/JSX as unsupported for TipTap and stays in **Raw**. Site Preview can still render it if the page is MDX; the in-editor rich preview will not.

So for “CTA anywhere” without losing the current markdown experience: put position in an ordered **sections** field, not in the markdown body.

<timestamp>Saturday, Nov 14, 2026, 6:46 PM (UTC+8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
Can there be a custom convention like a template language support in the tiptap editor
</user_query>
I'll check how TipTap is set up today and what a custom block/template convention would take.

Yes — but as a **small, allowlisted block convention**, not a general template language.

Today TipTap rich mode only round-trips a fixed Markdown set. Anything that looks like HTML/MDX (`<>`, `{}`, imports) fails `canRoundTrip` and stays Raw. So “full Liquid/Handlebars/MDX in TipTap” is a no. A **custom CTA node** that TipTap understands end-to-end is a yes.

What works well:

1. **Source convention** — something TipTap + Astro both know, e.g.
   ```md
   :::cta
   heading: Ready to launch?
   label: Get started
   href: /pricing
   :::
   ```
   or a fenced block: ` ```cta ` with YAML attrs.

2. **TipTap custom Node** — renders as a CTA card in the editor; slash command to insert; serialize/parse that exact syntax.

3. **Site renderer** — remark plugin or MDX component that turns the same syntax into the real CTA.

What does *not* work without a much bigger project: free-form `{{ ... }}`, arbitrary components, or “any template language.” You’d keep rejecting unknown tags so rich mode stays lossless.

**Tradeoff:** frontmatter ordered sections stay simpler and don’t touch the body editor. A TipTap convention is better if writers need the CTA **inside** article flow and still want rich editing.

If you want to go ahead, next step is picking one syntax (`:::cta` vs fenced vs shortcode) and whether Astro should parse it in `.md` or only `.mdx`.
